sources: PickHVAC – Goodman HVAC age: serial number decoding (pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/goodman)
PickHVAC – Amana HVAC age: serial number decoding (pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/amana)

Building Intelligence Center – Amana HVAC age (building-center.org/amana-hvac-age)
howtolookatahouse.com - How to determine the age of a Goodman furnace (9901 = January 1999)
notes: Digits 1-2 = year, digits 3-4 = month (01-12), digits 5-10 = production sequence. All ten characters are numeric; no letters.

Applies to Goodman, Amana (after the 1997 Goodman purchase), and Daikin-branded units built by Daikin Comfort Technologies / Goodman (DCG/DCC/DCH, DBG/DBC/DBH, DX/DZ splits, Daikin Fit). Not for Daikin Applied / McQuay or Japanese/Thai-built Daikin VRV.

Example dates above are the ones stated by the cited secondary decoders (1806 -> June 2018, 9704 -> April 1997, 02/11 -> Nov 2002) plus the 1509 -> Sept 2015 example from the pack brief; confidence held at medium because no manufacturer document or warranty lookup was checked in this session. Goodman's online warranty lookup (goodmanmfg.com) or the Daikin Comfort warranty lookup confirms the ship date from the serial.

Era: Goodman has used the same YYMM sequencing since it began building HVAC equipment (pickhvac.com: 'has used the same serial number sequencing for manufacture dates from the beginning'; howtolookatahouse.com gives 9901 = January 1999 with no era cutoff), so the era starts at Goodman's first HVAC production (1982). YY 82-94 collides with the McQuay legacy numeric format - the pack keeps both candidates (same date either way); disambiguate by the nameplate brand (Goodman/Amana/Janitrol logo vs McQuay logo and RPS/RDT/RAH model prefixes).

Amana units built before 1997 (Raytheon era) use different serial styles (a letter year code in the 7th position for 1980-82 and the 'BLACKHORSE' letter-digit cipher before the Goodman purchase per PickHVAC/building-center); those rules were not verifiable in this session and are not decoded here.

notes: Characters 1-4 are letters (plant / product code), characters 5-6 = year, 7-8 = month, remainder = sequence. building-center.org and hvacserialnumber.com / inspectorhandbook.com independently state the 5th-8th character YYMM rule. The four-letter prefix STNU appears on real McQuay chiller serials; its Staunton, VA meaning is inferred from McQuay's Staunton plant listing and is NOT confirmed - treat the plant field as advisory. An earlier revision of this pack spelled the prefix 'STOU' and listed 'FBOU' (Faribault, MN) from field memory; no source shows either, so they were removed from the map.

The worked examples are real serials quoted in secondary sources (STNU010600209 -> 2001-06; STNU130400198 -> 2013-04). Caution: fedequip.com states its STNU040200097 unit was 'built in 1997' while this rule gives 2004-02 - one listing conflicts with the rule, so always confirm real dates through Daikin Applied technical support or the unit's MFG DATE field, which most McQuay/Daikin Applied plates also print explicitly.
Era start is an estimate; McQuay used all-numeric serials before this style (see mcquay-legacy-numeric-yymm). Year is two-digit with pivot 70 (00-69 -> 2000s, 70-99 -> 1900s).

serialFormats.description: McQuay legacy all-numeric serial: YYMM in the first four digits (1971 to mid-1990s)
sources: Building Intelligence Center – McQuay HVAC age (building-center.org/mcquay-hvac-age): 'date of manufacture is coded in the 1st thru 4th digits of the serial number and represents the year and month of manufacture' (later format after the 1964-1970 letter style)

Collides with the Goodman/Amana 10-digit YYMM format for years 1982-1994 (both formats then decode the same YYMM, so no date ambiguity is flagged); the decoder drops this format for years >= 1995. A McQuay plate is easy to tell apart from a Goodman plate (McQuay/Daikin Applied logo, RPS/RDT/RAH model prefixes) - use the brand to pick the right format.

serialFormats.description: Daikin Industries (Japan/Thailand/Texas VRV and ductless) serial: one letter followed by six digits - date not decodable without Daikin's year chart

date.note: Daikin VRV / ductless serials do not carry a plain YYMM. The cited secondary pages describe other Daikin serial styles (building-center.org: 1970s/80s digit-year styles and a 1995-1999 style with a letter year in the 2nd position and a letter month in the 3rd; inspectorhandbook.com: letter = plant, digits 2-3 = year, 4-5 = month) that vary by product line and plant; none documents this one-letter + six-digit shape, so the engine reports the match but not a date. Use the Daikin Comfort / Daikin AC warranty lookup (daikincomfort.com or daikinac.com, enter the serial) or Daikin Comfort support at (866) 588-6454 to get the build date. faultCodes.meaning: Fault. Duct high limit (supply duct high static pressure switch) input opened - unit shut down and remains shut down until the fault is manually cleared through the unit keypad or via a network signal.
likelyCauses: Closed or stuck fire/smoke dampers, closed VAV boxes at start-up

Duct high-limit switch (DHL) set point too low or switch failed
Dirty filters combined with high fan speed

Verify VAV boxes/dampers open before fan start; check the SAF VFD ramp and duct static set point

Freezestat set too high
checks: Measure air temperature at the coil face and hot-water supply temperature; confirm valve stroke and pump/flow
Check the OA damper actuator drives closed on unit shutdown
Verify freezestat setting and continuity to the controller input
faultCodes.source: ED 15112 Table 40 value 252 'Freeze Fault'; OM 920 'Alarms' -> Faults; ED 15112 alarm point 'Freeze Fault'
faultCodes.notes: BAS Current Alarm value 252 ('Freeze Fault'). (BAS Current Alarm enumeration transcribed from ED 15112-20 Table 40 by one reader; confirm against the ED 15112 revision loaded on your BAS.)

faultCodes.meaning: Fault. 'An Emergency Stop Fault will occur if either of the following conditions is true' - the emergency stop digital input (24 VAC expected on the E-stop input; field smoke/fire/duct-high-temperature devices are wired in series) opens, or the network emergency stop command is received. Unit shut down until the input is restored and the alarm manually cleared.
likelyCauses: Field emergency-stop / fire-alarm relay contact open or missing factory jumper
Smoke detector, fire panel relay or duct high-temperature limit tripped
Broken field wiring / voltage drop through field devices so the input no longer sees a solid 24 VAC
BAS writing the network Emergency Override / Emergency Stop point
checks: Measure 24 VAC at the emergency-stop input terminals on the field terminal strip; jumper temporarily to prove the controller input (field practice)
Trace the field interlock chain (smoke detectors, fire alarm relay, shunt trip)
Check the BAS emergency-override/stop point value in ED 15112 before assuming a wiring fault
faultCodes.source: OM 920 'Alarms' -> Faults -> Emergency Stop Fault ('will occur if either of the following conditions is true'); ED 15112 Table 40 value 250; HVAC-Talk 'Daikin DPS Microtech 3 emergency stop Fault' (24 VAC on the DI, corroboration only)
faultCodes.notes: BAS Current Alarm value 250 ('Emergency Stop Fault'). (BAS Current Alarm enumeration transcribed from ED 15112-20 Table 40 by one reader; confirm against the ED 15112 revision loaded on your BAS.)

faultCodes.meaning: Problem class. 'This alarm occurs on units equipped with compressorized cooling only. If the high pressure switch opens indicating a high refrigerant pressure situation, the High Pressure Circuit 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 problem occurs.' The affected circuit's compressor(s) are disabled; the rest of the unit keeps running. Same alarm exists for circuits 2 through 6.
likelyCauses: Dirty or blocked condenser coil; condenser fan(s) not running or wrong rotation
Overcharge or non-condensables
Failed condenser fan motor / EC fan or fan VFD
HP switch failed or wiring open
checks: Compare discharge pressure to the HP switch trip point on the unit data plate; check condenser fan operation and rotation
Inspect condenser coil, clean if needed; check subcooling for overcharge
Ohm the HP switch and wiring to the expansion module input
faultCodes.source: OM 920 'Alarms' -> Problems -> High Pressure Circuit 1..6 (ManualsLib p.81); ED 15112 alarm points 'High Pressure Circuit 1..4 Problem'

faultCodes.meaning: Fault. 'When a Discharge Air Sensor fault occurs (after the Sensor Alarm Delay, default 30 seconds), the unit is shut down. It remains shut down until the Discharge Air Sensor fault is manually cleared through the unit keypad or via a network signal.'
likelyCauses: DAT sensor open or shorted (10k thermistor)
Sensor wiring damaged or unplugged at the MCB / expansion module analog input
Sensor removed from the discharge plenum during service and not reconnected
checks: Ohm the DAT sensor and compare with the thermistor table in OM 920 (10k at 77 F); inspect wiring
Confirm the sensor is on the correct analog input and the input is configured for the sensor type
Clear the fault after repair; the Sensor Alarm Delay (default 30 s) must elapse before it re-trips
faultCodes.notes: Because discharge temperature is the control variable for cooling and heating, MicroTech III treats a DAT sensor failure as a Fault (unit shut down) on rooftop units. BAS Current Alarm value 228 ('Discharge Sensor Fail'). (BAS Current Alarm enumeration transcribed from ED 15112-20 Table 40 by one reader; confirm against the ED 15112 revision loaded on your BAS.)
faultCodes.source: OM 920-1 / OM 920 'Alarms' -> Faults -> Discharge Air Sensor (McQuay MicroTech III RAH OM on ManualsLib); ED 15112 Table 40 value 228

faultCodes.meaning: Fault. 'An Airflow Fault occurs if differential pressure switch PC7 fails to detect airflow for longer than the airflow timer (default = 120 seconds) and on VAV units the current duct static pressure indication is less than half the static pressure setpoint after the unit leaves the Startup operating state or any time afterward, while the unit is running.' The unit is shut down and remains shut down until the fault is manually cleared through the unit keypad or via a network signal. (Older OM 920 / MicroTech II text calls the same alarm 'Fan Fail'.)
likelyCauses: Supply fan not running: VFD faulted or not enabled, fan contactor/overload open, broken belt, motor failure
PC7 airflow (fan-proving) differential pressure switch failed, tubing kinked/disconnected, or set point too high for the airflow
R63 fan-status relay contacts not making (PC7 is wired in series with R63 to DI1) - reported field cause
VAV units: duct static pressure transducer reading under half of set point (blocked pickup tube, transducer failure, closed dampers)
Airflow timer too short for a slow VFD ramp
checks: Confirm the supply fan actually runs when commanded (Manual Control / Unit Status); read any VFD fault code at the drive
With the fan running, verify PC7 closes: check its tubing to the blower section and jumper PC7 momentarily to prove the DI1 input (field practice)
Check the R63 relay coil/contacts in the PC7 circuit and 24 VAC at DI1
VAV: compare the displayed duct static to the set point; check the static pressure tubing and transducer
Clear the fault at Alarm Lists -> Active Alarms -> Clear Alarms once the cause is fixed
faultCodes.source: OM 920 'Alarms' -> Faults -> Airflow Fault (ManualsLib Daikin MicroTech III Operation Manuals p.84); ED 15112 Table 40 value 208 'Airflow Fault'; HVAC-Talk 'Daikin airflow fault' (PC7/R63 wiring, corroboration only)
faultCodes.notes: BAS Current Alarm value 208. (BAS Current Alarm enumeration transcribed from ED 15112-20 Table 40 by one reader; confirm against the ED 15112 revision loaded on your BAS.)

faultCodes.meaning: Fault. When the Low Discharge Air Temperature fault occurs the unit is shut down and remains shut down until the Low Discharge Air Temperature fault is manually cleared through the unit keypad or via a network signal.
likelyCauses: Heating failure in cold weather (gas furnace lockout, electric heat stages not energizing, hot-water valve/coil no flow) with outside air damper open
Economizer / outside-air damper stuck open or minimum position too high in low ambient
Discharge air sensor reading low (poor location in a cold plenum, partially failed thermistor)
Cooling running when it should not (compressor contactor welded, wrong mode)
checks: Compare the displayed DAT with a reference thermometer in the discharge plenum
Verify heat operates: furnace status/FSG lockout, electric heat contactors, hot-water valve stroke and supply temperature
Check outside-air damper actuator position and minimum OA set point against current ambient
Ohm the DAT thermistor (10k NTC) and inspect wiring to the MCB/expansion module input
faultCodes.source: OM 920 'Alarms' -> Faults -> Low Discharge Air Temperature (ManualsLib p.84); ED 15112 Table 40 value 212
faultCodes.notes: BAS Current Alarm value 212 ('Low Discharge Air Temp'). (BAS Current Alarm enumeration transcribed from ED 15112-20 Table 40 by one reader; confirm against the ED 15112 revision loaded on your BAS.)

faultCodes.meaning: Fault. Discharge air temperature above the high limit; unit shut down (Fault class - manual clear). The specific temperature threshold text was not visible in the sources seen; ED 15112 notes the enumeration text 'High'/'Low' Discharge Air Temp Fault.
likelyCauses: Heat running out of control: gas valve stuck open, electric heat contactor welded, hot-water/steam valve failed open
Low airflow across the heater (dirty filters, closed dampers, VFD at minimum) raising discharge temperature
DAT sensor drifted/shorted toward a high reading
checks: Verify the heat source de-energizes when the controller commands off (gas valve voltage, heat contactors, valve actuator)
Check airflow: filters, dampers, supply fan speed
Compare DAT display with a reference thermometer; ohm the thermistor
faultCodes.source: OM 920 'Alarms' -> Faults (High Discharge Temperature listed among faults); ED 15112 Table 40 value 216 'High Discharge Air Temp'
faultCodes.notes: BAS Current Alarm value 216 ('High Discharge Air Temp'). (BAS Current Alarm enumeration transcribed from ED 15112-20 Table 40 by one reader; confirm against the ED 15112 revision loaded on your BAS.)

faultCodes.meaning: Fault. Return air temperature above the high return limit; unit shut down (Fault class). On MicroTech II the equivalent 'Hi Return Tmp' fault shuts the unit down and it remains shut down until the fault is manually cleared through the unit keypad or via a network signal.
likelyCauses: Fire or abnormal heat source in the space/return plenum (this alarm is a smoke/fire safety function)
Return air sensor located near a heat source or shorted
Heat running with the return damper closed / recirculation of hot discharge air
checks: Treat as a potential fire/overheat condition first - inspect the space and return plenum
Compare the displayed RAT with a reference thermometer; ohm the RAT thermistor and wiring
Check for hot discharge air short-cycling into the return (open access panels, failed return damper)
faultCodes.source: ED 15112 Table 40 value 220 'High Return Air Temp'; OM 920 faults list ('High Return Temperature'); McQuay OM 137 MicroTech II 'Alarm Control - Faults' (Hi Return Tmp shutdown/manual clear text)
faultCodes.notes: BAS Current Alarm value 220 ('High Return Air Temp'). (BAS Current Alarm enumeration transcribed from ED 15112-20 Table 40 by one reader; confirm against the ED 15112 revision loaded on your BAS.)

faultCodes.meaning: Fault. 'A Control Temperature Fault that shuts down the unit is initiated if any of the following is true': the return air sensor is not present and reliable and Return Air is selected as the control temperature and a space sensor is not available; a network or local space sensor is not present and reliable and Space is selected as the control temperature and a return temperature sensor is not available; the OAT sensor is not present and reliable and Outdoor Air is selected as the control temperature; or the mixed air temperature sensor is not present or reliable and Mixed Air is selected as the control temperature. The unit remains shut down until the fault is manually cleared through the unit keypad or via a network signal.
likelyCauses: Return air / space / OAT / mixed-air sensor open or shorted while selected as Control Temp Source with no fallback sensor
Network space temperature not being written by the BAS (stale/NaN) with Control Temp Source = Space and no wired sensor
Wrong Control Temp Source selection for the sensors actually installed
checks: Check Commissioning/Unit Setup -> Control Temp Source and confirm the corresponding sensor reads a valid value on the Temperatures screen
Ohm the selected sensor (10k NTC) and its wiring; check Space Sensor Present setting
If BAS-supplied space temp is used, verify the network write is arriving (ED 15112 point) and not defaulting
faultCodes.source: OM 920 'Alarms' -> Faults -> Control Temperature Fault (ManualsLib p.84); ED 15112 Table 40 value 244
faultCodes.notes: BAS Current Alarm value 244 ('Control Temp Fault'). (BAS Current Alarm enumeration transcribed from ED 15112-20 Table 40 by one reader; confirm against the ED 15112 revision loaded on your BAS.)

faultCodes.meaning: Problem class. Low pressure switch on the circuit opened; that circuit's compressor(s) are disabled while the unit keeps running. On MicroTech II the equivalent 'Lo Pres-Ckt1' is 'a notification that the low refrigerant pressure switch has tripped and the unit could be low on refrigerant'; if it occurs three times between 2:00 a.m. of one day and 2:00 a.m. of the next, the alarm does not automatically clear the third time but must be manually cleared through the unit keypad or via a network.
likelyCauses: Low refrigerant charge / leak
Low airflow across the evaporator (dirty filters, iced coil, fan problem) or low load
Restricted filter-drier or TXV, closed liquid-line valve
Low ambient operation without low-ambient control; LP switch or wiring open
checks: Check suction pressure/temperature and superheat; look for ice on the evaporator
Leak-check and verify charge by subcooling (TXV) per the unit data plate
Verify airflow (filters, fan) and liquid-line restriction (temperature drop across drier)
Ohm the LP switch and wiring; check the reset count in the Alarm Log
faultCodes.source: ED 15112 Table 40 values 154-159 'Low Pressure Circ 1..6'; OM 920 'Alarms' -> Problems (Low Pressure Problem); McQuay OM 137 MicroTech II 'Lo Pres-Ckt1' description (three-strikes manual clear)
faultCodes.notes: BAS Current Alarm values 154-159 = Low Pressure circuits 1-6. (BAS Current Alarm enumeration transcribed from ED 15112-20 Table 40 by one reader; confirm against the ED 15112 revision loaded on your BAS.)

faultCodes.meaning: Problem class. Gas-furnace heating failure indicated by the flame safeguard (FSG) control on units with a CAV supply fan; 'the heat fail problem clears automatically when the FSG control is reset'. Unit continues to run; heating is unavailable until the FSG is reset.
likelyCauses: Furnace ignition failure / flame loss (FSG lockout): dirty flame rod, weak spark, gas pressure, gas valve
Furnace safeties open (high limit, rollout, combustion air proving/pressure switch)
FSG control or its wiring to the controller failed
checks: Read the FSG (flame safeguard) status/LED at the furnace and reset it; observe an ignition cycle
Check gas supply/manifold pressure, flame signal, and the combustion-air pressure switch
Verify the furnace limit and rollout switches are closed; the Heat Fail problem clears on FSG reset
faultCodes.source: OM 920 'Alarms' -> Problems -> Heat Fail Problem (ManualsLib p.81: 'clears automatically when the FSG control is reset'; occurs on units with a CAV supply fan)

faultCodes.meaning: Problem class. Outdoor air temperature sensor open or shorted (sensor not present and reliable). 'When the alarm condition is no longer present, the OAT Sensor problem automatically clears.' Functions that depend on OAT (economizer, reset, low-ambient lockouts) are disabled or revert: 'reset reverts from OAT to None when an Outdoor Air Sensor opens or shorts'.
likelyCauses: OAT thermistor open/shorted or wiring damaged (sensor is exposed in the outdoor hood/condenser section)
Sensor unplugged at the MCB analog input
Network OAT expected but not being written by the BAS
checks: Ohm the OAT sensor (10k NTC at 77 F) and wiring; compare the displayed OAT with actual ambient
Check the Network OAT / sensor source configuration
Problem clears automatically once the reading is valid
faultCodes.source: OM 920 'Alarms' -> Problems -> OAT Sensor Problem (ManualsLib p.81); McQuay MicroTech III RAH OM 'Reset - Cooling' section

faultCodes.meaning: Problem class. 'The MicroTech III controller generates a Space Temperature Sensor Problem alarm if the Space Sensor Present setting is set to Yes' and the space sensor is not present and reliable (open/short). Control falls back where a return sensor is available; 'reset reverts from Space to None when a Space Sensor opens or shorts'. Clears automatically when the reading is valid.
likelyCauses: Wall-mounted space sensor open/shorted or wiring damaged
Space Sensor Present = Yes but no sensor installed
Network space temperature not being written
checks: Ohm the space sensor (10k NTC) at the unit terminals; check for a valid Space Temp reading on the display
Set Space Sensor Present = No if no local sensor is fitted and control is by return/network
Verify BAS is writing the network space temperature point
faultCodes.source: OM 920 'Alarms' -> Problems -> Space Sensor Problem; OM 920 'Space Sensor Present' setting description; McQuay MicroTech III RAH OM 'Reset - Cooling'

faultCodes.meaning: Problem class (Rebel / variable-speed compressor units). 'If the variable speed compressor is operating and the discharge line temperature is greater than 250 F for 15 seconds, a High Discharge Line Compressor Problem alarm is generated'; normal compressor control is limited while the condition exists.
likelyCauses: Low charge / high superheat starving the inverter compressor
High condensing pressure (dirty condenser coil, condenser fan/EC fan problem, high ambient)
EEV not opening (stuck/failed stepper, sensor error) or liquid-line restriction
Discharge line thermistor drifted
checks: Read discharge line temperature, discharge superheat, suction pressure and superheat on the MicroTech III refrigerant status screens (gauges not required)
Check condenser coil cleanliness and condenser fan operation
Verify EEV position vs. command and superheat control; check charge by subcooling
Ohm the discharge line thermistor (inverter code J3 is the inverter-board equivalent sensor fault)
faultCodes.source: OM 920 'Alarms' -> Problems -> Hi DL Temp Problem (ManualsLib Daikin MicroTech III Operation Manuals p.81); Rebel IM 1125 / OM 1141 VFD compressor discharge-temperature limits

faultCodes.meaning: Problem class. Self-contained (SWP/SWT) units: the water flow switch input indicates no condenser water flow; compressor operation is disabled while the unit continues to run.
likelyCauses: Condenser water pump off / isolation valve closed / low flow
Flow switch paddle stuck or switch failed; wiring open
Strainer plugged
checks: Verify condenser water flow and pump status; check the water regulating valve position
Jumper the flow switch briefly to prove the input (field practice), then repair the switch/wiring
Clean strainers
faultCodes.source: ED 15112 Table 40 value 137 'Waterflow Sw' (problem); OM 920 self-contained alarms (SWP/SWT)
faultCodes.notes: Only the alarm name and class were visible in the sources seen; the description of what the switch monitors is standard self-contained practice, not quoted text. BAS Current Alarm value 137 ('Waterflow Sw'). (BAS Current Alarm enumeration transcribed from ED 15112-20 Table 40 by one reader; confirm against the ED 15112 revision loaded on your BAS.)

faultCodes.meaning: Problem class. Self-contained (SWP/SWT) units: alarm on the head-pressure water regulating valve control (valve/actuator feedback).
likelyCauses: Water regulating valve actuator failed or feedback out of range
Actuator wiring/power lost
Valve mechanically stuck
checks: Command the valve from Manual Control and watch position feedback
Check actuator power and signal wiring at the expansion module
Check condensing pressure against water flow
faultCodes.source: ED 15112 Table 40 value 140 'Water Regulating Valve' (problem)
faultCodes.notes: Only the alarm name and class were visible in the sources seen; causes/checks are field practice. BAS Current Alarm value 140 ('Water Regulating Valve'). (BAS Current Alarm enumeration transcribed from ED 15112-20 Table 40 by one reader; confirm against the ED 15112 revision loaded on your BAS.)

faultCodes.meaning: Warning. 'If the pressure drop across the filter section in the unit exceeds the setting of the differential pressure switch the Dirty Filter warning occurs. When the Dirty Filter warning occurs, unit operation is not affected. The Dirty Filter warning must be manually cleared through the unit keypad or via a network signal.'
likelyCauses: Filters loaded
Filter differential pressure switch set too low for the filter type/airflow, or tubing reversed/disconnected
Switch failed closed
checks: Inspect/replace filters
Check the filter DP switch set point and tubing (high side upstream of filters); measure filter pressure drop with a manometer
Clear the warning manually after service
faultCodes.source: OM 920 'Alarms' -> Warnings -> Dirty Filter (ManualsLib Daikin DPS IOM p.73 / OM 920); ED 15112 Table 40 value 24
faultCodes.notes: BAS Current Alarm value 24 ('Dirty Filter'). (BAS Current Alarm enumeration transcribed from ED 15112-20 Table 40 by one reader; confirm against the ED 15112 revision loaded on your BAS.)

faultCodes.meaning: Warning. The PC7 airflow switch indicates airflow when the fan is not commanded on (or fails to change state as expected); 'this normally indicates a problem with the PC7 airflow switch. When the Airflow Switch warning occurs, unit operation is not affected.' 'When the alarm condition is corrected, the Airflow Switch warning must be manually cleared through the unit.'
likelyCauses: PC7 differential pressure switch stuck closed or set too low (closes from building/duct pressure with the fan off)
Switch tubing reversed
R63 relay contacts welded
checks: With the supply fan off, verify PC7 is open and DI1 is de-energized
Check PC7 set point and tubing; replace if stuck
Clear the warning manually after repair
faultCodes.source: OM 920 'Alarms' -> Warnings -> Airflow Switch (ManualsLib Daikin DPS IOM p.73); ED 15112 Table 40 value 28
faultCodes.notes: BAS Current Alarm value 28 ('Airflow Sw'). (BAS Current Alarm enumeration transcribed from ED 15112-20 Table 40 by one reader; confirm against the ED 15112 revision loaded on your BAS.)

faultCodes.meaning: Warning. Self-contained (SWP/SWT) water-side warning; unit operation is not affected (Warning class).
likelyCauses: Condensate/water conductivity sensor reading out of range
Sensor fouled or wiring open
checks: Inspect the conductivity sensor and wiring; clean the sensor
Clear the warning after service
faultCodes.source: ED 15112 Table 40 value 32 'Conductivity' (warning)
faultCodes.notes: Only the alarm name and class were visible in the sources seen; verify the description against OM 920 self-contained section. BAS Current Alarm value 32 ('Conductivity'). (BAS Current Alarm enumeration transcribed from ED 15112-20 Table 40 by one reader; confirm against the ED 15112 revision loaded on your BAS.)

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter board fault code E5 - 'Inverter Compressor Motor Lock' (Rebel DPS variable-speed compressor drive).
likelyCauses: Compressor mechanically locked / seized
Compressor winding fault or wiring (U-V-W) miswired/open
Inverter PCB output stage fault
Liquid flood-back or oil issue at start
checks: Check compressor winding resistance and insulation; verify U/V/W wiring and connector seating
Check for high back-pressure / liquid at start; verify crankcase and oil boost operation
Follow the IM 1125 / OM 1263 E5 troubleshooting flow before replacing the inverter PCB
faultCodes.source: Rebel IM 1125 / OM 1263 Troubleshooting 'Inverter Board Fault Codes' - Error Code: E5 (ManualsLib Daikin MicroTech III DPS IOM p.76)

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter board fault code E7 - 'Malfunction of Outdoor Unit Fan Motor' (condenser fan motor / fan inverter).
likelyCauses: Condenser (outdoor) fan motor locked, seized bearing, or obstructed
Fan motor winding / connector fault
Fan inverter (drive) fault
checks: Spin the condenser fan by hand; check for obstruction and bearing drag
Check fan motor winding resistance and connector; check fan drive output
Follow the E7 troubleshooting flow in IM 1125 / OM 1263
faultCodes.source: Rebel IM 1125 / OM 1263 'Inverter Board Fault Codes' - Error Code: E7 (ManualsLib Daikin MicroTech III DPS IOM p.78)

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter board fault code H7 - 'Abnormal Outdoor Fan Motor Signal'.
likelyCauses: Condenser fan motor position/rotation signal (Hall) faulty
Fan motor connector or wiring fault
Fan motor or drive PCB failure
checks: Check the fan motor signal connector and wiring
Check fan motor per IM 1125 / OM 1263 H7 procedure
faultCodes.source: Rebel IM 1125 / OM 1263 'Inverter Board Fault Codes' - Error Code: H7 (ManualsLib Daikin MicroTech III DPS IOM)

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter board fault code L1 - 'Defective Inverter PC Board'.
likelyCauses: Inverter PCB internal fault (IGBT, current sensor)
Compressor short causing PCB damage
checks: Check compressor windings for shorts before replacing the PCB
Check power supply and DC bus; follow the L1 procedure in IM 1125 / OM 1263
faultCodes.source: Rebel IM 1125 / OM 1263 'Inverter Board Fault Codes' - Error Code: L1 (ManualsLib Daikin MicroTech III DPS IOM)

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter board fault code L4 - 'Malfunction of Inverter Radiating Fin Temperature Rise' (inverter heat-sink over-temperature).
likelyCauses: Inverter heat sink dirty / cooling airflow blocked
High ambient in the control compartment
Fin thermistor failed
checks: Clean the inverter heat sink and check cooling airflow across it
Check the fin thermistor resistance
Follow the L4 procedure in IM 1125 / OM 1263
faultCodes.source: Rebel IM 1125 / OM 1263 'Inverter Board Fault Codes' - Error Code: L4 (ManualsLib Daikin MicroTech III DPS IOM)

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter board fault code L5 - 'Momentary Overcurrent of Inverter Compressor' (instantaneous DC overcurrent).
likelyCauses: Compressor winding short / ground fault
Compressor lock or sudden load (liquid slugging)
Inverter PCB fault
checks: Megger and ohm the compressor windings; check U/V/W wiring
Check for liquid return/flooded start
Follow the L5 procedure in IM 1125 / OM 1263
faultCodes.source: Rebel IM 1125 / OM 1263 'Inverter Board Fault Codes' - Error Code: L5 (ManualsLib Daikin DPS IOM p.140)

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter board fault code L8 - 'Momentary Overcurrent of Inverter Compressor' (electronic thermal / sustained overcurrent).
likelyCauses: Compressor overload from high pressure / high load
Compressor winding or wiring fault
Low supply voltage
checks: Check compressor current vs. rating, discharge pressure and condenser operation
Check compressor windings and wiring; check supply voltage
Follow the L8 procedure in IM 1125 / OM 1263
faultCodes.source: Rebel IM 1125 / OM 1263 'Inverter Board Fault Codes' - Error Code: L8 (ManualsLib Daikin MicroTech III DPS IOM p.88)

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter board fault code U2 - 'Power Supply Insufficient or Instantaneous Failure' (DC bus under-voltage / momentary power loss).
likelyCauses: Supply voltage sag, phase loss or momentary outage
Loose power wiring / contactor chatter
Inverter DC bus capacitor or PCB fault
checks: Check three-phase supply voltage and balance at the inverter under load
Inspect power wiring and terminals for looseness
Follow the U2 procedure in IM 1125 / OM 1263
faultCodes.source: Rebel IM 1125 / OM 1263 'Inverter Board Fault Codes' - Error Code: U2 (ManualsLib Daikin MicroTech III DPS IOM p.98)

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter board fault code L9 - 'Inverter Compressor Starting Failure'.
likelyCauses: Compressor fails to start (locked, high differential pressure at start)
Compressor wiring/connector fault
Inverter PCB fault
checks: Check that pressures equalize before start; check compressor windings and wiring
Follow the L9 procedure in IM 1125 / OM 1263
faultCodes.source: Rebel IM 1125 / OM 1263 'Inverter Board Fault Codes' - ManualsLib 1423224 (Daikin MicroTech III DPS IOM) page title 'Error Code: L9 - Inverter Compressor Starting Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter board fault code H9 - 'Outdoor Air Thermistor Short/Open'.
likelyCauses: Inverter-side outdoor air thermistor open/shorted
Connector/wiring fault
checks: Ohm the thermistor and check its connector at the inverter PCB
Follow the H9 procedure in IM 1125 / OM 1263
faultCodes.source: Rebel IM 1125 / OM 1263 'Inverter Board Fault Codes' (code list summarized from ManualsLib Daikin MicroTech III DPS IOM troubleshooting section)

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter board fault code J3 - 'Compressor Discharge Pipe Thermistor Short/Open/Misplaced'.
likelyCauses: Discharge line thermistor open/shorted or fallen off the pipe
Connector/wiring fault
checks: Ohm the discharge thermistor; confirm it is strapped to the discharge line and insulated
Follow the J3 procedure in IM 1125 / OM 1263
faultCodes.source: Rebel IM 1125 / OM 1263 'Inverter Board Fault Codes' (code list summarized from ManualsLib Daikin MicroTech III DPS IOM troubleshooting section)

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter board fault code J5 - 'Suction Pipe Thermistor Short/Open'.
likelyCauses: Suction line thermistor open/shorted
Connector/wiring fault
checks: Ohm the suction thermistor and check its connector
Follow the J5 procedure in IM 1125 / OM 1263
faultCodes.source: Rebel IM 1125 / OM 1263 'Inverter Board Fault Codes' (code list summarized from ManualsLib Daikin MicroTech III DPS IOM troubleshooting section)

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter board fault code J6 - 'Outdoor Heat Exchanger Thermistor Short/Open'.
likelyCauses: Condenser coil thermistor open/shorted
Connector/wiring fault
checks: Ohm the coil thermistor and check its connector
Follow the J6 procedure in IM 1125 / OM 1263
faultCodes.source: Rebel IM 1125 / OM 1263 'Inverter Board Fault Codes' (code list summarized from ManualsLib Daikin MicroTech III DPS IOM troubleshooting section)

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter board fault code LC - 'Communication Error between Outdoor Control PCB and Inverter PCB'.
likelyCauses: Communication cable between the refrigerant control board and the inverter PCB loose/damaged
Inverter PCB or control PCB fault; power supply to the inverter PCB
checks: Check the communication harness and connectors between the boards; check inverter PCB power LED
Follow the LC procedure in IM 1125 / OM 1263
faultCodes.source: Rebel IM 1125 / OM 1263 'Inverter Board Fault Codes' (code list summarized from ManualsLib Daikin MicroTech III DPS IOM troubleshooting section)

faultCodes.meaning: MicroTech II legacy Problem. 'Lo Pres-Ckt1 is a notification that the low refrigerant pressure switch has tripped and the unit could be low on refrigerant.' 'If the Lo Pres-Ckt1 problem occurs three times between 2:00 a.m. of one day and 2:00 a.m. of the next, the alarm does not automatically clear the third time but must be manually cleared through the unit keypad or via a network.' Same for Lo Pres-Ckt2.
likelyCauses: Low refrigerant charge / leak
Low evaporator airflow or iced coil
Restriction (drier, TXV); LP switch/wiring open
checks: Check suction pressure and superheat; leak-check and verify charge
Check filters/airflow and liquid-line restriction
Count occurrences in the alarm log; manual clear after the third
faultCodes.source: McQuay OM 137 / OM 138 MicroTech II Applied Rooftop Unit Controller 'Alarm Control' -> Problems (ManualsLib McQuay MicroTech II Operation Manual)

faultCodes.meaning: MicroTech II legacy Problem. Evaporator frost protection switch (FP2, opens at 30 F, closes at 45 F) tripped: 'When the Frost-Ckt2 problem occurs, the unit continues to operate but cooling circuit #2 is disabled.' Same for Frost-Ckt1 / FP1.
likelyCauses: Low evaporator airflow (dirty filters, closed dampers, fan speed) or low load causing coil frosting
Low charge / low suction pressure
Frost protection switch failed or wiring open
checks: Check for ice on the evaporator; verify airflow and filters
Check suction pressure/superheat and charge
Ohm FP1/FP2 (return bends of the evaporator) and wiring to the circuit board input; check hot-gas-bypass operation if fitted
faultCodes.source: McQuay OM 137 / OM 138 MicroTech II 'Alarm Control' -> Problems (Frost-Ckt2 text); RoofPak IM 893 component list (FP1, 2 frost protection switches open at 30 F, close at 45 F)

faultCodes.meaning: MicroTech II legacy Fault. High return air temperature: the unit is shut down and remains shut down until the fault is manually cleared through the unit keypad or via a network signal (same shutdown/manual-clear text applies to the MicroTech II 'Space Sensor', 'Return Sensor' and 'Disch Sensor' faults).
likelyCauses: Fire/overheat in the space or return plenum
Return sensor shorted or near a heat source
checks: Inspect for a fire/overheat condition first
Compare RAT display with a reference thermometer; ohm the sensor
faultCodes.source: McQuay OM 137 MicroTech II Applied Rooftop Unit Controller 'Alarm Control' -> Faults (ManualsLib p.91)

diagnosticTips: Full alarm table (Faults / Problems / Warnings with descriptions and reset behaviour) is in OM 920 'Alarms' and the model-specific OM (Rebel OM 1141 / Maverick II OM 1294 quick start); the BAS point names are in ED 15112 (protocol information).
Software level is shown under About This Unit; note it when calling Daikin Applied technical support.

Display: 4-line LCD on the main control board (MCB) in the unit control compartment, navigated with the push-and-roll wheel (rotate to move, press to select). Main Menu -> Alarm Lists -> Active Alarms (priority order, highest first) and Alarm Log (history with time stamps). 'About This Unit' shows software version - note it before calling Daikin Applied technical support (800-432-1342).

Alarm classes (OM 920): Faults shut the unit down and must be cleared manually (keypad or network); Problems limit operation (e.g. one refrigerant circuit or heating disabled) while the unit keeps running - some clear automatically when the condition ends, some (e.g. third Low Pressure trip in a day) need a manual clear; Warnings are informational and do not affect operation (Dirty Filter and Airflow Switch warnings must be cleared manually).

Clearing: Alarm Lists -> Active Alarms -> Clear Alarms = Clear (or the BAS Clear Alarm point). Alarms clear only if the condition that caused them no longer exists; per OM 1141 alarms are also cleared when power is cycled. ED 15112 cautions against repeated network writes to the clear-alarm point.

BAS alarm numbering (ED 15112 Table 40 'Current Alarm'): 0 = No Active Alarms; Warnings 1-99 (24 Dirty Filter, 28 Airflow Sw, 32 Conductivity); Problems 100-199 (137 Waterflow Sw, 140 Water Regulating Valve, 154-159 Low Pressure Circ 1-6); Faults 200-255 (208 Airflow Fault, 212 Low Discharge Air Temp, 216 High Discharge Air Temp, 220 High Return Air Temp, 224 Duct High Limit, 228 Discharge Sensor Fail, 244 Control Temp Fault, 250 Emergency Stop Fault, 252 Freeze Fault). Use these when a BAS shows only the number. Values transcribed from ED 15112-20 Table 40 by one reader (only 212 = Low Discharge Air Temp was independently seen in a search snippet); ED 15112 has revisions -7 through -20 - confirm the numbering against the revision loaded on your BAS.
Sensor faults have a Sensor Alarm Delay (default 30 s) before they trip. All temperature sensors are 10k NTC thermistors (about 10k ohms at 77 F) - the resistance table is in OM 920.

Key digital inputs to check with a meter: PC7 airflow switch (in series with fan-status relay R63) proves supply fan airflow on DI1 - the Airflow Fault is the most common shutdown; the Emergency Stop input expects a solid 24 VAC through the field smoke/fire/duct-high-temperature devices - a voltage drop through a field device is enough to trip it.

Manual / test operation: Commissioning -> Manual Control (later software) or Unit Status/Unit State screens let you command the supply fan, compressors, condenser fans, dampers and heating for testing; cooling and heating can be enabled/disabled under Commissioning. On Rebel (inverter compressor) units, refrigerant pressures, superheat and subcooling are read on the controller screens - gauges are not required at start-up.

Rebel DPS inverter compressor: the drive protects itself (discharge temp 275 F shutdown, discharge superheat limits, high-pressure switch 580 psig, oil boost) and reports 2-character inverter board fault codes (E5, E7, H7, L1, L4, L5, L8, U2 ...) - troubleshooting flowcharts for each are in IM 1125 / OM 1263 'Inverter Board Fault Codes'.

Network module LEDs: BSP LED = module-to-controller state (green normal, flashing red firmware error, solid red hardware error); BUS LED = module-to-network state (green OK, red not communicating). BACnet MS/TP settings (MAC, baud, Device Instance) are under the BACnet/LON setup menu; the unit must be power-cycled after changing them.

Communication module LEDs: IM 917 / IM 916 also document further BSP/BUS LED states (e.g. yellow/orange) beyond the green/red states listed here; their exact meaning was not captured - consult the LED tables in the module IM (low confidence).

ledPatterns.pattern: Communication module (BACnet MS/TP IM 917, BACnet IP IM 916, LonWorks) BSP LED - solid GREEN
ledPatterns.meaning: Normal: the module's board support package is running and communication is established between the communication module and the unit controller.
checks: No action for the BSP LED; if the network is still down, look at the BUS LED

ledPatterns.pattern: Communication module BSP LED - flashing RED
ledPatterns.meaning: Firmware error on the communication module ('if the BSP LED is flashing RED, then the firmware has an error').
checks: Power-cycle the unit controller with the module seated; reload module firmware per OM 1085 / IM 917 if it persists; replace the module

ledPatterns.pattern: Communication module BSP LED - solid RED
ledPatterns.meaning: Hardware error on the communication module ('if it is solid RED, then there is a hardware error').
checks: Reseat the module on the MCB connector; check 24 VAC to the MCB; replace the module

ledPatterns.pattern: Communication module BSP LED - alternating RED/GREEN
ledPatterns.meaning: Application software upgrade in progress on the communication module (IM 917 BSP LED table).
checks: Wait for the firmware load to finish, then power-cycle the unit controller if the LED does not return to solid green

ledPatterns.pattern: Communication module BUS LED - solid GREEN
ledPatterns.meaning: Communication between the module and the BACnet/LON network is running (network OK).
checks: No action

ledPatterns.pattern: Communication module BUS LED - solid RED
ledPatterns.meaning: 'The unit controller is not capable of communicating to the network' - no valid network communication (wrong MS/TP baud/MAC/address, wiring, or no BAS traffic).
checks: Check MS/TP polarity, termination and shield; verify MAC address, baud rate and Device Instance under the BACnet setup menu; confirm the BAS is polling

controls.name: McQuay MicroTech II applied rooftop unit controller (RPS, RFS, RCS, RPR, RFR, RDT, RDS, RAR, RAH c. 2001-2010)

faultCodes.meaning: Space temperature sensor failed while the controller depends on it - the unit is shut down until the alarm is manually cleared.
likelyCauses: Space sensor open/shorted or unplugged
Control Temperature Source set to Space while no sensor is installed
Field wiring damaged
checks: Ohm the space sensor (10k thermistor) and wiring at the controller analog input
Check Control Temp Source setting; change to Return if no space sensor is used, then clear the alarm
faultCodes.source: McQuay OM 137 MicroTech II Applied Rooftop Unit Controller Operation Manual - Alarm Control / Faults (manualslib 1326625 p.91)

faultCodes.meaning: Return air temperature sensor failed - the unit is shut down until the alarm is manually cleared.
likelyCauses: Return air sensor open/shorted
Wiring or connector fault at the controller analog input
checks: Ohm the RAT sensor and compare to the thermistor table; check the plug at the controller
Clear the alarm after repair (Faults do not auto-clear)
faultCodes.source: McQuay OM 137 MicroTech II Applied Rooftop Unit Controller Operation Manual - Fault Alarms (manualslib 1341639 p.111)

Faults must be cleared manually from the keypad Alarm menu (or via the network Clear Alarm point) after the cause is fixed; Problems and Warnings clear automatically when the condition ends.

controls.name: Goodman / Amana / Daikin (Goodman-built) integrated ignition control - single-LED flash codes (CPG/DCG/GPG packaged gas units and matching furnaces)
controls.description: Integrated hot-surface ignition control (Goodman part families PCBBF1xx / PCBBF13x, White-Rodgers 50-series OEM boards) with a single red diagnostic LED; the flash count identifies the fault. The exact table is printed on the unit's control-compartment door label - always read that label for the specific board. Enrichment pass 2026-09-26 via WebSearch summaries only (WebFetch blocked). Codes are grouped: CPG/DCG HSI single-LED table (incl. White-Rodgers 50A55/50M56 board fault index), GPG/APG M-series DSI 'Ignition Control Diagnostic Indicator Chart' (suffixed '(DSI chart ...)' to avoid clashing with the HSI table), ComfortNet furnace status codes E0-EA, ComfortNet blower codes b0-b9 and network/shared-data codes d0-d4. Contradiction on record: Goodman's own M-series installation manuals print a chart with 1 flash = Internal Control Failure and 2 flashes = External Lockout, while the narrative text in the same manuals (GPG16: 5 flashes = flame with valve closed; 7 flashes = limit opened 5 times) and GHAC's GPG14 note (1 flash = 3 failed ignition attempts) follow the furnace-style numbering. faultCodes.meaning: Internal control fault in the integrated ignition control - hard lockout; or no power to the control.
likelyCauses: Failed integrated control board
No 24 VAC to the control (transformer, fuse, door switch)
Loose low-voltage plug
checks: Verify 24 VAC at the control's R-C terminals and line voltage at L1-N
Cycle power for more than 5 seconds; if the LED stays off with power present, replace the control
faultCodes.source: Goodman CPG Series installation instructions - Diagnostic LED chart (manualslib 61600); White-Rodgers 50M56-743 fault index ('Off: control failure')

faultCodes.meaning: External lockout - retries or recycles exceeded (failed ignition attempts or flame dropouts). The control resets automatically after one hour, or reset by removing the thermostat call or interrupting power for more than five seconds.
likelyCauses: Low gas pressure or gas valve not opening
Dirty/cracked hot surface ignitor or poor flame sensor signal
Flame rectification problem (dirty flame rod, poor burner ground)
Burner/crossover problems causing flame dropouts
Per the CPG manual: also check the secondary limit and rollout limit and the wiring
checks: Watch the ignition sequence: inducer -> pressure switch -> HSI glow -> gas valve 24 V -> flame
Measure supply and manifold pressure (typ. 3.5 in. w.c. NG) and 24 V at the gas valve during trial for ignition; inspect orifices for debris (CPG manual)
Measure flame current (microamps DC) and clean the flame sensor; check ignitor resistance
faultCodes.source: Goodman CPG Series installation instructions - Diagnostic LED chart and Abnormal Operation - Heating (manualslib 61600); Daikin DCG Service Instructions (manualslib 1642558); White-Rodgers 50M56-743 fault index

faultCodes.meaning: Pressure switch stuck open - pressure switch did not close with the induced draft blower running. (CPG/DCG packaged-unit label. NOTE: White-Rodgers 50A55/50M56 furnace-style boards and Goodman furnace boards use 2 flashes for 'pressure switch stuck closed' - read the door label.)
likelyCauses: Faulty pressure switch or wiring
Disconnected, cracked or plugged pressure-switch hose
Blocked or restricted flue / vent, or condensate in the hose
Faulty or weak induced draft blower
checks: Confirm the inducer runs; measure inducer negative pressure at the switch tap with a manometer against the switch rating
Inspect the hose and flue outlet; check switch contacts close (0 V across the switch) with the inducer running
faultCodes.source: Goodman CPG Series installation instructions - Diagnostic LED chart (manualslib 61600)

faultCodes.meaning: Pressure switch stuck closed - the pressure switch is closed before the induced draft blower is energized; the control auto-resets after one hour or by removing power. (CPG/DCG packaged-unit label. NOTE: White-Rodgers 50A55/50M56 and Goodman furnace boards use 3 flashes for 'pressure switch stuck open'.)
likelyCauses: Faulty (welded) pressure switch
Faulty wiring shorting the switch input
checks: With the unit idle, check for continuity across the pressure switch; it should be open
Inspect the switch wiring for a short to 24 V
faultCodes.source: Goodman CPG Series installation instructions - Diagnostic LED chart (manualslib 61600); Daikin DCG Service Instructions 'Pressure Switch Stuck Closed (3 flash code)' (manualslib 1642558)

faultCodes.meaning: Open thermal protection device - the primary limit (or auxiliary limit / rollout circuit) is open.
likelyCauses: Dirty filter or excessive duct static (insufficient airflow)
Indoor blower not running or wrong speed; belt slipping on belt-drive units
Faulty limit switch
Open rollout switch (manual reset) on boards where rollout is in the limit string
checks: Measure external static and temperature rise against the data plate; check filters, blower speed/belt
Check continuity across each limit and rollout switch; reset any manual-reset rollout only after finding the cause
faultCodes.source: Goodman CPG Series installation instructions - Diagnostic LED chart (manualslib 61600); White-Rodgers 50M56-743 fault index ('4 flashes: open high temperature limit switch')

faultCodes.meaning: Flame detected with the gas valve de-energized (flame sensed when it should not be); the combustion and air circulator blowers are energized. Resets by removing power, or automatically after one hour.
likelyCauses: Gas valve leaking through / stuck open
Flame sensor circuit shorted or moisture on the control
Residual flame from a slow-closing valve
checks: Confirm 0 V at the gas valve while flame is present; if flame persists with no valve voltage, replace the gas valve
Check the flame sensor wiring for shorts to ground
faultCodes.source: Goodman CPG Series installation instructions - Diagnostic LED chart (manualslib 61600); Daikin DCG Service Instructions (manualslib 1642558); GPG 16 M Series installation 'Flame Detected with Gas Valve Closed - five (5) flashes'

faultCodes.meaning: Igniter relay fault / shorted hot surface igniter (some boards omitted this code from the door label - see Goodman Service Bulletin SF-024 'Missing Identification of Eight (8) Flash Fault Code'). SF-024: 'According to the control manufacturer, the eight (8) Flash Fault Code indicates an igniter relay fault or a shorted HSI. However, field indications have linked this fault code to either an open or insufficient grounding of the furnace.'
likelyCauses: Open or poor equipment ground / reversed line polarity (SF-024 field finding)
Shorted or grounded hot surface igniter
Failed igniter relay on the integrated control
checks: Verify a low-impedance ground from the control chassis to the service ground and L1/N polarity before replacing the igniter or board
Disconnect the igniter and measure its resistance (typically 40-90 ohms for silicon nitride/carbide types per the unit label) and check for a short to ground
If the ground and the igniter are good, replace the control
faultCodes.source: Goodman Service Bulletin SF-024 - Missing Identification of Eight (8) Flash Fault Code (mobile.goodmanmfg.com Tech Services); White-Rodgers 50M56-743 fault index ('8 flashes: ignitor relay fault'); corroborated by third-party flash-code guides

faultCodes.meaning: Model-dependent. CPG packaged-unit chart: 'Short Cycle Compressor Delay' (Daikin DCG service manual: 'compressor output delay or short cycle compressor delay'). White-Rodgers 50A55/50M56 furnace-style boards: 'Open rollout switch'. Read the door label for the board fitted.
likelyCauses: CPG/DCG: normal anti-short-cycle timing after a cooling call is satisfied or interrupted (not a fault)
WR boards: flame rollout switch tripped by flame rollout (blocked heat exchanger/flue, low combustion air, burner misalignment)
checks: CPG/DCG: wait out the compressor delay; if the unit never restarts, check the thermostat call, the compressor contactor coil and any external time-delay/phase monitor
WR boards: check the manual-reset rollout switch continuity; find and correct the cause of rollout before resetting
faultCodes.source: Goodman CPG Series installation instructions - Diagnostic LED chart (manualslib 61600); Daikin DCG Service Instructions (manualslib 1642558, 6 blinks); White-Rodgers 50M56-743 fault index ('6 flashes: open rollout switch')

faultCodes.meaning: Board-dependent. White-Rodgers 50A55/50M56 fault index: 'Low flame sense current' (unit keeps running, warning). Goodman GPG 16 M Series installation instructions: if the primary limit opens five (5) times within the same call for heat, the ignition control locks out for one (1) hour and the red diagnostic LED flashes seven (7) times.
likelyCauses: Low flame signal: coated/dirty flame sensor, poor burner ground, lazy flame from low gas pressure or misaligned burner
Repeated limit trips: restricted airflow (filters, static, blower speed/belt), failing limit switch, over-fired unit
checks: Measure flame current in microamps DC and compare with the board's minimum; clean the flame rod with fine abrasive and check the ground path
If the limit has been cycling, check temperature rise, external static, blower operation and manifold pressure before clearing the lockout
Which meaning applies depends on the board: read the label on the control-compartment door
faultCodes.source: White-Rodgers 50M56-743 fault index ('7 flashes: low flame sense current'); Goodman GPG 16 M Series installation instructions - Abnormal Operation - Heating (seven flashes after five limit trips); third-party Goodman furnace guides corroborate 'low flame signal'

faultCodes.meaning: Reversed polarity (115 VAC line/neutral reversed at the control). White-Rodgers 50A55/50M56 fault index: 'Rapid flash: reversed polarity'.
likelyCauses: L1 and neutral swapped at the unit disconnect, junction box or board plug
Poor or missing equipment ground (flame rectification depends on it)
checks: Measure hot-to-ground (~120 V) and neutral-to-ground (~0 V) at the control's line plug; correct the wiring
Verify a solid ground wire from the board/burner assembly to the unit chassis and the supply ground
faultCodes.source: White-Rodgers 50M56-743 installation instructions - fault index p.8 (manualslib 1585345); White-Rodgers 50A55 troubleshooting manual (manualslib 556709)

faultCodes.meaning: Internal Control Failure - per the Ignition Control Diagnostic Indicator Chart in the A/GPG13, APG14/GPG14 and GPG16 M-series installation instructions (direct-spark PCBAG boards). NOTE: the narrative text of the same manuals and third-party GPG14 notes describe 1 flash as lockout after three failed ignition attempts - confirm on the control-compartment door label.
likelyCauses: Failed direct-spark ignition control (PCBAG12x/PCBAG127)
Ignition lockout after retries (if the label for this board assigns 1 flash to external lockout)
checks: Cycle 24 V power to the board for more than 5 seconds; if 1 flash returns immediately with no call for heat, replace the control
If the label says 1 flash = failed ignition, check spark at the electrode, spark gap, gas pressure and flame sense before condemning the board
faultCodes.source: Goodman A/GPG13 M Series installation instructions - Ignition Control Diagnostic Indicator Chart p.25 (manualslib 798533); Goodman APG14 M Series installation instructions p.33 (manualslib 2325520); GPG 16 M Series installation instructions (acdirect PDF). Conflict noted from GHAC KB entry 758 'GPG14 - Flashing Code 1: 3 Failed Ignition Attempts'

faultCodes.meaning: External Lockout - per the Ignition Control Diagnostic Indicator Chart (A/GPG13, APG14/GPG14, GPG16 M-series). The control repeats the ignition routine three times if combustion is not established, then shuts off the induced draft blower and goes into lockout.
likelyCauses: No spark or weak spark (electrode gap, cracked ceramic, high-voltage lead)
Gas valve not opening, low supply/manifold pressure, plugged orifices
Flame not proven (dirty flame sensor, poor ground, burner misalignment)
checks: Observe the sequence: inducer -> pressure switch -> spark (22,000 V DSI) -> gas valve 24 V -> flame proven
Check spark electrode gap/condition and flame-sense microamps; measure manifold pressure
Reset by removing the thermostat call or interrupting power for more than 5 seconds; auto-resets after one hour
faultCodes.source: Goodman A/GPG13 M Series installation instructions - Ignition Control Diagnostic Indicator Chart p.25 and Ignition Control Error Codes p.15 (manualslib 798533); Goodman APG14 M Series installation instructions p.33

faultCodes.meaning: Pressure Switch Stuck Open - per the Ignition Control Diagnostic Indicator Chart (A/GPG13, APG14/GPG14, GPG16 M-series).
likelyCauses: Pressure switch hose blocked, pinched or disconnected
Blocked flue / combustion air inlet, weak or failed induced draft blower
Incorrect switch set point or failed switch contacts; loose wiring
checks: With the inducer running, read inducer negative pressure at the switch tap with a manometer and compare with the switch rating
Check the switch closes (0 V across it) and the wiring to the board
faultCodes.source: Goodman A/GPG13 M Series installation instructions - Ignition Control Diagnostic Indicator Chart p.25 (manualslib 798533); Goodman APG14 M Series installation instructions p.33 (manualslib 2325520)

faultCodes.meaning: Pressure Switch Stuck Closed - per the Ignition Control Diagnostic Indicator Chart (A/GPG13, APG14/GPG14, GPG16 M-series).
likelyCauses: Welded/failed pressure switch contacts
Wiring short to 24 V on the switch input
checks: With the unit idle (inducer off) verify the switch is open; replace if closed
Inspect switch wiring for shorts
faultCodes.source: Goodman A/GPG13 M Series installation instructions - Ignition Control Diagnostic Indicator Chart p.25 (manualslib 798533); Goodman APG14 M Series installation instructions p.33 (manualslib 2325520)

faultCodes.meaning: Thermal Protection Device Open - per the Ignition Control Diagnostic Indicator Chart (A/GPG13, APG14/GPG14, GPG16 M-series). The limit opening de-energizes the burners and powers the air circulation and vent blowers until the limit closes.
likelyCauses: Restricted airflow (dirty filter, closed registers, high external static, wrong blower speed)
Failed primary/auxiliary limit or open manual-reset rollout switch
Over-firing (manifold pressure or orifice size)
checks: Measure temperature rise against the data plate and external static; correct airflow first
Check continuity through each limit and the rollout switch(es); reset rollout only after finding the cause
faultCodes.source: Goodman A/GPG13 M Series installation instructions - Ignition Control Diagnostic Indicator Chart p.25 (manualslib 798533); GHAC KB entry 631 'GPG13 - Flashing Code 4' describes the limit-open behavior (corroboration)

faultCodes.meaning: Flame Detected with Gas Valve Closed - per the Ignition Control Diagnostic Indicator Chart in the Goodman GPG13 installation instructions. (The GPG16 M-series narrative assigns this condition five flashes - confirm on the door label.)
likelyCauses: Gas valve leaking through / slow closing
Flame sensor circuit shorted or moisture on the control
checks: Confirm 0 V at the gas valve while flame persists; replace the valve if flame continues
Check the flame sensor lead for shorts to ground; dry/clean the control if wet
faultCodes.source: Goodman GPG13 Installation & Operating Instructions - Ignition Control Diagnostic Indicator Chart (manualslib 483769); GPG 16 M Series installation (five flashes variant)

faultCodes.meaning: High-stage pressure switch circuit will not close during high-stage induced draft blower operation (two-stage boards only).
likelyCauses: Pinched, blocked or mis-routed high-stage pressure switch hose
Blocked flue or combustion air inlet; inducer not reaching high speed
Loose wiring or failed high-stage pressure switch
checks: Run the unit on high stage (W2) and measure inducer pressure at the high-stage switch tap against its rating
Verify the inducer changes speed on high stage and the switch closes; check wiring to the board
faultCodes.source: Third-party Goodman flash-code guides (doityourself.com, appliancehelper.net, afmplumbingheating.com) for the two-stage PCBAG127 board; not seen verbatim in the GPG14 service manual RS6300012 during this pass

faultCodes.meaning: LOCKOUT DUE TO EXCESSIVE RETRIES (ComfortNet communicating furnace status code).
likelyCauses: Failed ignition attempts: dirty flame sensor, low gas pressure, gas valve not opening, cracked igniter
Flame dropouts during the cycle
checks: Clear by interrupting power for 30 seconds (or remove the call for heat); watch the next ignition sequence
Clean the flame sensor, measure flame microamps, and check 24 V at the gas valve during trial for ignition
faultCodes.source: Goodman GMVC950704CX / CVC9/95 installation instructions - Status Codes (manualslib 1084722 p.58, 836277 p.52)

faultCodes.meaning: LOW STAGE PRESSURE SWITCH STUCK CLOSED AT START OF HEATING CYCLE (ComfortNet furnace status code).
likelyCauses: Welded low-stage pressure switch contacts
Wiring short on the switch input
checks: With the inducer off, confirm the low-stage switch is open; replace if closed
Inspect wiring for shorts to 24 V
faultCodes.source: Goodman GMVC950704CX / CVC9/95 installation instructions - Status Codes

faultCodes.meaning: LOW STAGE PRESSURE SWITCH STUCK OPEN (ComfortNet furnace status code).
likelyCauses: Blocked, pinched or disconnected pressure switch hose; condensate in hose
Blocked vent/intake or drain; weak induced draft blower
Incorrect switch set point or failed switch; loose wiring
checks: Measure inducer pressure at the switch tap with a manometer against the switch rating
Inspect vent, intake and condensate trap; verify the switch closes with the inducer running
faultCodes.source: Goodman GMVC950704CX / CVC9/95 installation instructions - Status Codes

faultCodes.meaning: HIGH LIMIT OPEN - primary limit or auxiliary limit circuit is open, or rollout limit circuit is open (ComfortNet furnace status code).
likelyCauses: Restricted airflow (filter, static, blower speed)
Failed limit switch; tripped manual-reset rollout switch
checks: Check temperature rise and external static; correct airflow
Check continuity of primary, auxiliary and rollout limits; find the cause before resetting a rollout
faultCodes.source: Goodman GMVC950704CX / CVC9/95 installation instructions - Status Codes

faultCodes.meaning: IMPROPER FLAME - flame sensed with no call for heat (ComfortNet furnace status code).
likelyCauses: Gas valve leaking through or slow to close
Flame sensor circuit shorted
checks: Confirm 0 V at the gas valve while flame is present; replace the valve if flame persists
Check the flame sensor wiring for shorts
faultCodes.source: Goodman GMVC950704CX / CVC9/95 installation instructions - Status Codes

faultCodes.meaning: OPEN FUSE - displayed when the board's low-voltage fuse is open (ComfortNet furnace status code).
likelyCauses: Short in the 24 V thermostat or accessory wiring
Shorted humidifier/condensate pump or other 24 V load
checks: Find the short before replacing the 3 A automotive fuse: disconnect thermostat and accessory wires and check for shorts to ground
Replace the fuse only with the same rating
faultCodes.source: Goodman GMVC950704CX / CVC9/95 installation instructions - Status Codes

faultCodes.meaning: WEAK FLAME - flame sense microamp signal is low (ComfortNet furnace status code).
likelyCauses: Coated/dirty flame sensor, poor burner ground
Lazy flame from low gas pressure or misaligned burner
checks: Measure flame current (microamps DC); clean the flame rod and check the ground path
Check manifold pressure and burner alignment
faultCodes.source: Goodman GMVC950704CX / CVC9/95 installation instructions - Status Codes

faultCodes.meaning: IGNITOR FAULT OR IMPROPER GROUNDING (ComfortNet furnace status code).
likelyCauses: Open or shorted hot surface igniter
Missing/poor equipment ground; reversed polarity
checks: Measure igniter resistance and check for a short to ground
Verify hot/neutral polarity and a solid ground at the control
faultCodes.source: Goodman GMVC950704CX / CVC9/95 installation instructions - Status Codes

faultCodes.meaning: HIGH STAGE PRESSURE SWITCH STUCK CLOSED AT START OF HEATING CYCLE (ComfortNet furnace status code).
likelyCauses: Welded high-stage pressure switch contacts
Wiring short on the high-stage switch input
checks: With the inducer off, confirm the high-stage switch is open
Inspect wiring for shorts
faultCodes.source: Goodman GMVC950704CX installation instructions - Status Codes (manualslib 1084722 p.58)

faultCodes.meaning: High stage pressure switch stuck open (ComfortNet two-stage furnace status code). Confirm on the furnace door label.
likelyCauses: Blocked, pinched or mis-routed high-stage pressure switch hose
Blocked vent/intake, weak inducer, incorrect switch set point
checks: Run high stage and measure inducer pressure at the high-stage switch tap against its rating
Verify the inducer reaches high speed and the switch closes
faultCodes.source: Goodman GMVC950704CX installation instructions 'Status Codes' (manualslib 1084722 p.58): E9 causes 'pressure switch hose blocked, pinched...; blocked flue...; weak induced draft blower; incorrect pressure switch set point'; justanswer.com GMVC96/GMVC95 E9 threads (corroboration only)

faultCodes.meaning: REVERSED 115 VAC POLARITY - polarity of 115 volt AC power to the furnace or integrated control module is reversed (ComfortNet furnace status code).
likelyCauses: L1 and neutral swapped at the disconnect or junction box
Poor or missing ground
checks: Measure hot-to-ground (~120 V) and neutral-to-ground (~0 V) at the board line plug; correct the wiring
Verify the equipment ground
faultCodes.source: Goodman GMVC950704CX installation instructions - Status Codes (manualslib 1084722 p.58)

faultCodes.meaning: BLOWER MOTOR NOT RUNNING (ComfortNet blower fault code).
likelyCauses: No line voltage to the ECM/variable-speed motor
Motor control failure, failed motor
Loose motor communication/power plug
checks: Verify line voltage at the motor power plug and the low-voltage/communication plug is seated
Command a fan-only call and check for motor response; replace the motor/control if powered and commanded but not running
faultCodes.source: Goodman Diagnosis Code Identification System (mobile.goodmanmfg.com faultcodes); Goodman AVPTC**14 installation instructions - Diagnostic Codes p.31

faultCodes.meaning: BLOWER MOTOR COMMUNICATION ERROR (ComfortNet blower fault code).
likelyCauses: Loose or damaged motor communication harness
Failed motor control module or board
checks: Reseat the motor communication plug at the motor and board; inspect for damaged pins
Cycle power; if b1 persists with a good harness, check the motor control module
faultCodes.source: Goodman Diagnosis Code Identification System (mobile.goodmanmfg.com faultcodes); Goodman AVPTC**14 installation instructions - Diagnostic Codes p.31

faultCodes.meaning: BLOWER MOTOR HP MISMATCH - blower motor horsepower does not match the unit's shared data (ComfortNet blower fault code).
likelyCauses: Wrong replacement motor installed
Wrong shared data loaded on the board (memory card mismatch)
checks: Compare the motor part number/HP with the unit parts list
Reload the correct shared data with the unit's memory card
faultCodes.source: Goodman AVPTC**14 installation instructions - Diagnostic Codes p.31 (manualslib 1289171)

faultCodes.meaning: BLOWER MOTOR OPERATING IN POWER, TEMP., OR SPEED LIMIT (ComfortNet blower fault code).
likelyCauses: High external static pressure (undersized duct, dirty filter/coil)
High motor temperature from restricted airflow or high ambient
checks: Measure external static; clean filter and coil, open dampers/registers
Check motor temperature and airflow settings
faultCodes.source: Goodman AVPTC**14 installation instructions - Diagnostic Codes p.31 (manualslib 1289171)

faultCodes.meaning: BLOWER MOTOR CURRENT TRIP OR LOST ROTOR (ComfortNet blower fault code).
likelyCauses: Blower wheel binding or obstructed
Failed motor bearings or motor control
checks: Spin the blower wheel by hand for binding; check for debris
Verify line voltage; replace the motor/control if it trips repeatedly with a free wheel
faultCodes.source: Goodman Diagnosis Code Identification System (mobile.goodmanmfg.com faultcodes); Goodman AVPTC**14 installation instructions - Diagnostic Codes p.31

faultCodes.meaning: BLOWER MOTOR ROTOR LOCKED (ComfortNet blower fault code).
likelyCauses: Seized motor bearings
Blower wheel jammed
checks: Remove power and try to turn the wheel; clear obstructions or replace the motor
faultCodes.source: Goodman AVPTC**14 installation instructions - Diagnostic Codes p.31 (manualslib 1289171)

faultCodes.meaning: OVER/UNDER VOLTAGE TRIP OR OVER TEMPERATURE TRIP (ComfortNet blower fault code).
likelyCauses: Line voltage outside the motor's range (brownout, loose neutral)
Motor overheating from restricted airflow
checks: Measure line voltage at the motor under load and compare with the nameplate
Check airflow/static and motor ventilation
faultCodes.source: Goodman AVPTC**14 installation instructions - Diagnostic Codes p.31 (manualslib 1289171)

faultCodes.meaning: INCOMPLETE PARAMETER SENT TO MOTOR (ComfortNet blower fault code).
likelyCauses: Communication noise or a loose harness during motor programming
Corrupt or missing shared data on the board
checks: Cycle power; reseat the motor communication plug
Reload shared data from the unit's memory card if the code returns
faultCodes.source: Goodman AVPTC**14 installation instructions - Diagnostic Codes p.31 (manualslib 1289171)

faultCodes.meaning: LOW INDOOR AIRFLOW (minor error code) - the blower cannot deliver the requested CFM (ComfortNet blower fault code).
likelyCauses: Dirty filter or coil, closed registers, undersized ductwork (high static)
Blower speed/airflow setting too high for the duct system
checks: Measure external static and compare with the blower table; clean filter/coil
Check the airflow/trim settings on the thermostat or DIP switches
faultCodes.source: Goodman AVPTC**14 installation instructions - Diagnostic Codes p.31 (manualslib 1289171)

faultCodes.meaning: DATA NOT ON NETWORK - the unit is wired as part of a communicating system and the integrated control module does not contain any shared data (data not yet on network).
likelyCauses: New or replacement control board never loaded with shared data
Memory card not installed or not read
checks: Install the unit's shared-data memory card in the board's card slot and power up; wait for the data to load
If the card was already used, order the correct memory card for the exact model
faultCodes.source: Goodman ComfortNet ASXC/DSXC/GSXC Service and Troubleshooting RS6215001r7; Goodman Diagnosis Code Identification System (mobile.goodmanmfg.com faultcodes)

faultCodes.meaning: Unit is wired as part of a communicating system and the outdoor unit requires airflow greater than the indoor unit's airflow capability; shared data is incompatible with the system or missing parameters.
likelyCauses: Mismatched indoor/outdoor equipment (indoor blower cannot deliver the outdoor unit's required CFM)
Wrong shared data loaded for the indoor or outdoor unit
checks: Verify the indoor/outdoor match is an approved AHRI combination
Reload the correct shared data from each unit's memory card
faultCodes.source: Goodman ComfortNet ASXC/DSXC/GSXC Service and Troubleshooting RS6215001r7

faultCodes.meaning: Shared data sent to the integrated control module does not match the hardware configuration.
likelyCauses: Memory card for a different model was used
Replacement board or motor of a different configuration
checks: Compare the memory card part number with the unit model; load the correct card
Verify installed motor/board match the parts list
faultCodes.source: Goodman ComfortNet ASXC/DSXC/GSXC Service and Troubleshooting RS6215001r7

faultCodes.meaning: Shared data on the memory card has been rejected (invalid memory card data).
likelyCauses: Corrupt or wrong memory card
Card removed before the load completed
checks: Power down, reseat the card, power up and wait for the load to complete
Replace the memory card with the correct part if it is rejected again
faultCodes.source: Goodman ComfortNet ASXC/DSXC/GSXC Service and Troubleshooting RS6215001r7; Goodman AVPTC**14 installation instructions - Diagnostic Codes ('Invalid Memory Card Data')

ledPatterns.meaning: Normal operation, no fault stored (most Goodman integrated controls).
checks: If the unit does not run with a steady LED, check the thermostat call and 24 V at the control terminals

ledPatterns.meaning: Model-dependent: reversed 115 VAC line polarity / poor ground on some controls, open rollout switch on others - read the door label for this board.
checks: Verify L1/N polarity and a solid ground at the control
Check rollout switch continuity

ledPatterns.meaning: No power to the control or internal control failure (White-Rodgers fault index 'Off: control failure'; CPG chart 'internal fault - hard lockout').
checks: Verify line and 24 V at the board; if present and the LED stays off after a >5 s power cycle, replace the control

ledPatterns.meaning: Reversed 115 VAC polarity (White-Rodgers 50A55/50M56 fault index). Flash cadence for coded faults on these boards is ~0.25 s on per flash with a ~2 s pause between groups; an internal failure lights the LED continuously.
checks: Check hot/neutral polarity and ground at the control line plug

ledPatterns.pattern: Two-digit code on a dual 7-segment display (E0-EA, b0-b9, d0-d4)
ledPatterns.meaning: ComfortNet/ComfortBridge communicating control: alphanumeric status code shown on the board; the same fault is also sent as plain text to the CTK04 communicating thermostat.
checks: Read the code on the board and cross-check the plain-language message and fault history on the thermostat (Menu > Equipment Status > Diagnostics)

diagnosticTips: The diagnostic LED is on the integrated control board in the gas-heat control compartment; view it through the window in the blower/control door on packaged units.
Lockouts (1 and 5 flashes) auto-reset after one hour; clear immediately by removing the thermostat call for a few seconds or by interrupting power for more than 5 seconds.
The control retries ignition (typically 3 trials) before a 1-flash lockout; flame dropouts during a cycle count as recycles.

Flash-code tables differ between board generations (single-stage vs two-stage, 40-flash/blink-pattern boards on newer furnaces). The 6 and 7 flash meanings differ by board (CPG chart vs White-Rodgers 50-series vs DSI chart) - see the per-code notes and read the door label.

A phase monitor may be fitted on some 3-phase units (field or factory) - check the control compartment; a unit that is dead with a normal ignition-control LED may be locked out by it (check incoming phase rotation and voltage balance). Otherwise the CPG IOM relies on verifying supply-fan rotation at start-up to prove compressor rotation - there is no documented factory phase monitor.

The red diagnostic LED is on the integrated ignition control in the gas-heat control compartment; on packaged units view it through the window in the blower/control door. Count flashes between the ~2-second pauses.

Lockouts (external lockout, flame with valve closed, repeated limit trips) auto-reset after one hour; clear immediately by removing the thermostat call for a few seconds or by interrupting power for more than 5 seconds. ComfortNet furnaces: interrupt power for 30 seconds or clear the fault history from the thermostat.
The control retries ignition three times before an external lockout; flame dropouts during a cycle count as recycles.

Two different flash tables exist on Goodman packaged units: (a) CPG/DCG hot-surface-ignition boards (White-Rodgers 50-series style): 1 = external lockout, 2 = PS stuck open, 3 = PS stuck closed, 4 = limit open, 5 = flame with valve closed, 6 = short-cycle compressor delay; (b) GPG13/GPG14/GPG16 M-series direct-spark PCBAG boards: 1 = internal control failure, 2 = external lockout, 3 = PS stuck open, 4 = PS stuck closed, 5 = thermal protection device open, 6 = flame with valve closed. Goodman furnaces and the White-Rodgers universal 50A55/50M56 reverse the 2/3 pressure-switch codes (2 = stuck closed, 3 = stuck open). Always read the flash-code label on the control-compartment door.

ComfortNet/ComfortBridge units: the board shows a two-character code on a dual 7-segment display; the CTK04 thermostat stores the last 6 equipment faults - press MENU > EQUIPMENT STATUS > DIAGNOSTICS to view or clear fault history (the ComfortNet User Menu is password-protected with the date code printed on the back of the thermostat or shown under Equipment Status). The thermostat also logs the most recent 25 alerts with date/time.

ComfortNet d0/d2/d3/d4 codes are shared-data problems: a replacement control board must be loaded from the unit's memory card (insert the card, power up, wait for the load) before the equipment will run.
Direct-spark (DSI) GPG/APG boards fire a 22,000 V spark and prove flame with a separate flame sensor; check spark gap/ceramic and flame microamps before condemning the PCBAG board.
